_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Hungary covering Magyar conquest (Honfoglalás ~895 CE, Carpathian Basin), Kingdom of Hungary (Saint Stephen I, crowned 1000, Christianisation), Mongol invasion 1241, Ottoman occupation (Battle of Mohács 1526, 150 years), Habsburg rule, 1848 Revolution (Kossuth), Austro-Hungarian Empire (Compromise/Ausgleich 1867), WWI, Treaty of Trianon 1920 (lost 72% territory, national trauma), Horthy regency, WWII (Holocaust, 600k Hungarian Jews murdered), 1956 Revolution (Soviet crushed), Göulásh communism (Kádár), 1989 democratic transition, EU 2004, Orbán era.

religion.note: Historically Catholic but significant Reformed/Calvinist minority (eastern Hungary, 'Calvinist Rome' = Debrecen); Ottoman era destroyed Catholic institutions in many areas; communist era secularisation; Jewish community historically largest per capita (~800k before Holocaust, ~100k today, Budapest); Orbán promotes 'Christian values' as political identity

ethnic_groups.name: Hungarian (Magyar)
ethnic_groups.notes: Finno-Ugric language (isolated in Europe, related only to Finnish/Estonian distantly); unique national identity; Trianon trauma (millions of Hungarians left outside borders: Romania 1.2M, Slovakia 460k, Serbia 250k, Ukraine 150k); irredentism; puszta (Great Plain) identity

ethnic_groups.name: Roma
ethnic_groups.notes: Official 3.2%, estimated 5-8% (many don't declare); deeply marginalised; segregation in schools/housing; poverty; discrimination; activist movements growing; Orbán government controversial policies

ethnic_groups.name: German
ethnic_groups.notes: Danube Swabians/Saxons; expelled after WWII (200k+ deported); remaining community in Baranya/Tolna; cultural revival; minority self-government

ethnic_groups.name: Slovak
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Hungary; Békés County; national minority rights

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Croatian, Romanian, Serbian, Ukrainian minorities; Jewish (~100k, mostly Budapest, largest in Central Europe); large diaspora (1956 exodus ~200k, mainly US/Canada/Australia)

independence.from: Kingdom established (Stephen I crowned by Pope Sylvester II); modern: 1918-11-16 (republic); 1989-10-23 (Third Republic declared)

country_profile.notes_unique: Treaty of Trianon (June 4, 1920, Hungary lost 72% of territory and 64% of population to successor states, deepest national trauma, 'Nem, nem, soha!' / 'No, no, never!', still on every Hungarian's mind); 1956 Revolution (October 23, students/workers rose against Soviet control, Nagy declared neutrality, Soviets crushed with tanks, ~2,500 dead, 200k fled, inspired world); Rubik's Cube (Ernő Rubik, Budapest, best-selling toy in history ~450M sold); thermal baths (Budapest 'City of Spas', 123 thermal springs, Széchenyi largest in Europe); Hungarian diaspora geniuses ('The Martians': Szílárd, Teller, von Neumann, Wigner — Manhattan Project); paprika/goulash/Tokaji wine; 13 Nobel laureates (most per capita among medium nations); Orbán's 'illiberal democracy' (since 2010, media control, judicial reform, anti-immigration, EU clashes, Russia ties, blocking Ukraine sanctions, Article 7 triggered); CEU forced to leave (Soros university moved to Vienna)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Viktor Orbán
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Fidesz; longest-serving current EU leader; five terms total (1998-2002, 2010-present); started as liberal anti-communist (1989 speech demanding Soviet withdrawal), pivoted to national-conservative; 'illiberal state' model; supermajority since 2010; border fence 2015 (anti-migration); Soros conspiracy theories; EU funds frozen; close to Putin (blocked sanctions); media empire loyal; constitutional changes; Central European University expelled; Tucker Carlson favourite; CPAC speaker; EU's most controversial leader

head_of_state.name: Tamás Sulyok
head_of_state.title: President
head_of_state.notes: Former Constitutional Court president; replaced Katalin Novák who resigned (pardoned convicted child abuse enabler, scandal); largely ceremonial; Fidesz-aligned

former_leaders.name: Viktor Orbán (first term)
former_leaders.notes: First stint; youngest PM at 35; centre-right transformation from liberal origins; lost to Socialists 2002; rebuilt Fidesz stronger

former_leaders.name: Péter Medgyessy
former_leaders.notes: MSZP; ex-finance minister; revealed as former intelligence operative; resigned amid coalition tensions

former_leaders.name: Ferenc Gyurcsány
former_leaders.notes: MSZP; leaked 'őszödi beszéd' speech (2006, admitted lying to win election: 'We lied morning, noon and night', sparked riots); 2008 financial crisis hit Hungary hard; IMF bailout; paved way for Orbán's supermajority

former_leaders.name: János Kádár
former_leaders.notes: Communist era; installed by Soviets after 1956 revolution (betrayed Nagy); 'Goulash communism' (most liveable Eastern Bloc, 'Happiest Barrack'); gradual liberalisation; New Economic Mechanism 1968; died 1989 as system collapsed

former_leaders.name: Imre Nagy
former_leaders.notes: Communist reformer; declared Hungarian neutrality and withdrawal from Warsaw Pact during 1956 Revolution; captured by Soviets; executed 1958 (show trial); reburied 1989 (200k mourners, catalyst for regime change); national hero

910.name: Pannonia & the Migrations Era
910.description: The Carpathian Basin was the Roman province of Pannonia, then a migration corridor for Huns, Gepids, Avars, and Slavic peoples. The Avar Khaganate dominated for 250 years before Frankish and Slavic successor polities emerged.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Pannonia
sub_clusters.description: The Roman province of Pannonia, with Aquincum (Budapest) as its capital, served as a crucial Danubian frontier (limes). Significant Roman urban and military infrastructure, Christianity's early spread, and the Hunnic invasion under Attila.

920.name: Magyar Conquest & Árpád Kingdom
920.description: The Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin (honfoglalás, 895/896) under Árpád founded the Hungarian state. St. Stephen I's Christianisation (1000), the Mongol invasion (1241), and the extinction of the Árpád dynasty (1301) shaped medieval Hungary.

sub_clusters.name: Magyar Conquest & Western Raids
sub_clusters.description: Árpád's conquest of the Carpathian Basin, Magyar raids terrifying Western Europe from Italy to Spain, and the decisive defeat at the Battle of Lechfeld (955) by Otto I, ending the raiding era.

920.name: Angevin & Late Medieval Hungary
920.description: The Angevin dynasty and Matthias Corvinus brought Hungary to its peak of medieval power. Hungary became Central Europe's wealthiest kingdom under Charles I's gold-based economy and Matthias's Renaissance court.

sub_clusters.name: Angevin Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: Charles I Robert's gold currency reform and Louis the Great's expansion — Hungary became the largest gold producer in Europe. The Personal Union with Poland (1370–1382) extended Hungarian influence.

930.name: Ottoman Occupation & Habsburg Reconquest
930.description: The catastrophic defeat at Mohács (1526) led to 150 years of Ottoman occupation of central Hungary. The kingdom was tripartite-divided between Ottomans, Habsburgs, and the Transylvanian Principality, until Habsburg reconquest in the 1680s–90s.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of Mohács & Tripartite Partition
sub_clusters.description: The disastrous Battle of Mohács (August 29, 1526), where King Louis II was killed, led to Ottoman conquest of Buda (1541) and Hungary's division into three parts: Ottoman Hungary, Royal (Habsburg) Hungary, and the Principality of Transylvania.

940.name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise & Dual Monarchy
940.description: The Ausgleich (Compromise) of 1867 created the Dual Monarchy of Austria-Hungary, granting Hungary internal autonomy. Rapid industrialisation, Budapest's golden age, ethnic tensions with national minorities, and the catastrophe of WWI.

sub_clusters.name: Dual Monarchy & Budapest's Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Compromise gave Hungary self-government. Budapest was unified (1873), the Hungarian Parliament building constructed, the Millennium celebrations (1896), and rapid industrial and cultural development made Budapest a major European capital.

sub_clusters.description: Growing tensions with Slavic, Romanian, and other minorities. Hungary entered WWI as part of the Central Powers, suffering enormous casualties. The collapse of the Dual Monarchy and the armistice (November 1918) ended the old order.

950.name: Trianon, Interwar Period & WWII
950.description: The Treaty of Trianon (1920) stripped Hungary of two-thirds of its territory and one-third of ethnic Hungarians. Irredentist revisionism dominated the Horthy era. Alliance with Nazi Germany brought temporary gains but ended in catastrophic defeat and the Holocaust.

sub_clusters.name: Treaty of Trianon & Horthy Era
sub_clusters.description: The brief Soviet Republic under Béla Kun (1919), Miklós Horthy's authoritarian regency, the Treaty of Trianon (June 4, 1920) — the defining trauma of modern Hungarian history — and the Vienna Awards (1938, 1940) recovering Slovak and Transylvanian territories.

950.description: Soviet-imposed communist rule, Rákosi's Stalinist terror, the heroic 1956 Hungarian Uprising crushed by Soviet tanks, Kádár's subsequent 'goulash communism' allowing limited economic liberalisation, and the gradual opening that preceded the 1989 transition.
